releases.description:
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and Procurement Act 2023 do not apply to this award. The standstill period begins on the day after the publication of this notice. Representations by providers must be made to decision makers by midnight on Wednesday the 18th November 2026. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award under the PSR.
Written representations should be sent to donna.iley@durham.gov.uk
Officers of Public Health Senior Management Team and Adult and Health Senior Management were the decision makers.
There were no Conflicts of interest identified among the Decision Makers.
The council has fully considered each of the key criteria when making a decision on the award of this contract. A particular emphasis was placed upon:
Key criterion 1: Quality and innovation
HDFT consistently delivers strong performance across the 0-25 Family Health Service. Robust governance and data-quality arrangements are in place. Quality and safety remain strong, with routine monitoring of incidents and complaints, low levels of formal escalation and consistently positive service-user feedback. HDFT continues to invest in quality improvement, supporting service development, evaluation and continuous improvement. 
Key criterion 2: Value
The service supports over 150,000 children and young people, providing universal and targeted support in response to significant levels of need and health inequality across County Durham. HDFT demonstrates financial responsibility through transparent monthly reporting on staffing and workforce pressures and has reduced its management fee over the contract term, supporting continued cost efficiency.
Key criterion 3: Integration, collaboration and service sustainability
HDFT works effectively with Public Health, Early Help, Children's Social Care, Maternity Services and Family Hubs, supporting integrated pathways and a consistent "no wrong door" approach for families.
HDFT responds collaboratively to system change and emerging need through joint pathways, strengthened referral arrangements and active participation in strategic public health partnerships.
Key criterion 4: Access, inequalities and choice
HDFT supports access and reduces inequalities through a tiered model of universal, enhanced and targeted provision, enabling early identification of need and preventative support.
Services are delivered flexibly across homes, community venues, Family Hubs and schools, supported by digital provision including a 24/7 health app, online resources and practitioner-led health chat.
Key criterion 5: Social value
HDFT has exceeded social value expectations through local employment, apprenticeship learning and volunteering activity, supporting local workforce and community development.

tender.title: CHS - Acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) Contract Extension
tender.description:
Croydon Health Services NHS Trust intends to extend its existing contract with Oracle Health for the provision of its acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system for a further three years, with an option to extend for an additional 12 months.

The extension will maintain continuity of the Trust’s existing clinical digital services, including the core EPR software, application management, hosting and associated support services. The existing system is integral to the Trust's clinical workflows and digital infrastructure, with significant technical dependencies and integration requirements.

The proposed arrangements include the removal of certain existing functionality and the introduction of additional integrated functionality, including Blood Transfusion Administration and Milk Management modules, to support the Trust's clinical and operational requirements. These modules require integration with the existing EPR environment, making technical compatibility, interoperability and continuity of clinical services key considerations.

The Trust is also progressing plans for a future competitive procurement of its EPR requirements, with the proposed extension providing continuity of existing services during this period.

lots.description:
Croydon Health Services NHS Trust proposes to extend its existing contract with Oracle Health for the provision of its acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system, commencing on 29th December 2026 for an initial period of three years, with an option to extend for a further 12 months.

The proposed arrangements cover the continued provision of the core EPR software and associated clinical applications, application management, hosting, software licensing, maintenance and technical support services. These services support the Trust's existing clinical and operational activities and the integration of the EPR with other systems across its digital infrastructure.

The proposed arrangements also incorporate changes to the existing scope, including the removal of certain voice recognition, in-application training and user guidance functionality. Additional requirements include increased system user capacity, enhanced application management support, upgrade management services, and further integrated clinical functionality supporting blood transfusion administration and milk management to meet the Trust's operational requirements. A trial of AI-enabled clinical functionality will also be included to evaluate its potential benefits and inform the Trust's future EPR requirements.

The existing EPR operates within a complex and highly integrated technical environment, with established interfaces, clinical workflows and dependencies across the Trust’s wider digital infrastructure. The additional functionality must operate effectively and safely within this environment, maintaining compatibility with the core EPR platform and associated clinical systems.

Introducing an alternative supplier at this stage would present significant technical and interoperability challenges, including the need for additional integration, configuration, testing, clinical safety assurance and ongoing support arrangements. This could create disproportionate technical difficulties and operational risks to established clinical services, alongside unnecessary duplication of implementation, integration and support costs. Continuing with the incumbent supplier will preserve compatibility with the existing EPR environment and enable the proposed requirements to be delivered through established technical and operational arrangements.

The proposed three-year extension, with an option for a further 12 months, reflects the complexity of maintaining and supporting a highly integrated clinical system while accommodating the Trust’s naturally evolving clinical and operational requirements. The optional fourth year recognises the complexity of a major clinical system procurement and transition, providing for circumstances where additional time may be required to complete implementation, data migration and associated integration activities while maintaining continuity of essential clinical services.

The Trust is separately progressing its longer-term EPR strategy, which will include a competitive procurement for its longer-term EPR requirements. The proposed extension is intended to maintain continuity of the existing EPR environment throughout the competitive procurement process, and support implementation and transition to the future arrangements.

The estimated total value of the proposed extension, including the optional fourth year, is approximately £17,549,439 excluding VAT.

options.description: The Trust has the option to extend the contract for a further 12 months following the initial three-year extension period.  The optional fourth year recognises the complexity and timescales associated with a major clinical system procurement and transition, allowing additional time, if required, for implementation, data migration and integration activities whilst maintaining continuity of essential clinical services.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
Croydon Health Services NHS Trust intends to extend its existing contract with Oracle Health for the continued provision of its acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system, on the grounds of technical compatibility, interoperability and the significant technical and operational difficulties associated with introducing an alternative supplier at this stage.

The existing Oracle Health EPR is an established and highly integrated clinical system, supporting essential patient care and operational activities across the Trust. It is embedded within clinical workflows and connected to other clinical and operational systems through established interfaces, data flows and supporting infrastructure. The continued operation of this environment requires compatibility between the core EPR platform, associated applications, hosting arrangements and ongoing application management and support services.

The current contract expires on 28th December 2026. Introducing an alternative EPR supplier within the remaining contractual period would require substantial technical and operational activity, including system configuration, development and testing of interfaces, data migration, validation, clinical safety assurance and the implementation of revised clinical workflows. These activities would need to be undertaken in a planned and controlled manner to protect the integrity and availability of patient information and maintain continuity of essential clinical services. It would not be practicable to complete such a transition before expiry of the existing arrangements.

The proposed extension also incorporates adjustments to the existing services, including additional user capacity, application management and upgrade management services, together with integrated clinical functionality - these requirements are closely connected to the existing EPR environment. Introducing alternative suppliers to deliver these elements separately would create additional technical dependencies and interoperability challenges, potentially requiring further interfaces, configuration, testing and separate support arrangements. Such an approach could result in disproportionate technical difficulties and significant economic inefficiencies, including duplication of implementation, integration, licensing and support costs. It could also necessitate maintaining parallel technical arrangements while the Trust continues to operate and support its existing EPR platform.

The proposed extension with Oracle Health will maintain continuity of the established EPR environment and enable the associated requirements to be delivered within the existing technical and operational arrangements, avoiding the disproportionate disruption and duplication of costs associated with introducing alternative provision at this stage.

The Trust is separately progressing its longer-term EPR strategy, which will include a competitive procurement for its future EPR requirements. The proposed extension is intended to maintain continuity of essential clinical services throughout that process and support implementation and transition to the future arrangements.

tender.description:
Mini Competition on Fusion 21 Building Safety and Compliance Framework Lot 1 for asbestos surveying 
Competition for work to award TWO suppliers for the provision of asbestos surveys, sampling, air monitoring, training and reinspection's across a 20,000‑property housing portfolio. Be One Homes subcontracts all asbestos‑related activities and requires TWO suitably qualified and accredited suppliers capable of delivering the full scope of services (both Stream 1 and Stream 2), including Management Surveys, Refurbishment and Demolition (R&D) Surveys, sample collection and analysis, air monitoring, four‑stage clearances, and cyclical reinspections undertaken on a 1‑, 2‑ or 3‑year basis. 
Service delivery will operate across two defined streams: 
Stream 1: All asbestos surveys, sampling and air monitoring within tenanted properties, including all properties subject to scheduled reinspections. Also, asbestos surveys associated with the Capital Programme where can deliver to agreed timescales.  
Stream 2: All asbestos surveys, sampling and air monitoring within void and care & repair properties, together with the delivery of asbestos training. Also, asbestos surveys associated with the Capital Programme where can deliver to agreed timescales.

tender.description: Health promotion, prevention and support service, complementing GUM provision, to promote good sexual health: reduce the prevalence of STI, increase uptake of LARC. Core elements include YP, sex workers, those living with HIV.

lots.description:
The commissioning responsibility for sexual and reproductive health services sits with local authorities under the Health and Social Care Act 2012. Westminster City Council and the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea have jointly commissioned the Sexual Health Promotion, Prevention and Support Service since 2017 to address health inequalities and improve sexual health outcomes for residents.
The service has the following aims:
Provide accessible, confidential promotion, prevention and support services across both boroughs. 
Deliver targeted interventions for priority and disproportionately affected groups, including young people, LGBTQ+ communities, ethnic minority groups, people with learning disabilities, people living with HIV, and individuals at risk of exploitation. 
Strengthen community based engagement, outreach and digital delivery to increase reach, reduce stigma and support early intervention. 
Improve integration and pathways with clinical sexual health providers, primary care, mental health, substance misuse and other key services. 
Support behaviour change and resilience through peer mentoring, asset‑based approaches and community partnerships. 
Promote healthy relationships, consent and safety, reducing harm associated with sexual exploitation, violence and poor sexual health literacy. 
This notice sets out the intention to award a contract following a competitive procurement process under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR).
The proposed contract term is five years from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032, with an option to extend for two further one-year periods to 31 March 2034.

tender.title: FA08-14 Chemical Dosing
tender.description:
The scope of the frameworks allows for a number of suppliers to provide Chemical Dosing services and expertise in relation to off-site build, minor site works and temporary hire.
Lot 1 - Off-site Build - 
The scope includes the survey, design, manufacture, testing and supply of package plant dosing systems, incorporating chemical storage and dosing equipment housed within GRP or alternative material kiosks, together with associated building services. 
Lot 2A - Northumbrian Water Operating Region and Lot 2B Essex & Suffolk Operating Region - 
The scope includes the provision of low-complexity and minor works services for existing chemical dosing and related assets across the North East and Essex & Suffolk operating regions. This includes refurbishment, modification, relocation and ad hoc maintenance activities at water and wastewater treatment facilities, pumping stations, boreholes and service reservoirs. Suppliers will provide the expertise and resources required to support the ongoing operation and performance of existing assets, delivering works efficiently and cost-effectively while supporting innovation and carbon reduction objectives.
Lot 3 - Temporary Hire -
1.7.1.	The scope includes the provision of temporary hire chemical dosing package plants to support operational requirements, emergency response, planned maintenance activities and process trials across the Northumbrian Water and Essex & Suffolk Water operating areas. Suppliers can provide both standard and bespoke dosing solutions, designed as fully automated, reliable and resilient plug-and-play systems. The scope includes the supply of containerised or kiosk-based dosing units incorporating pumps, pipework, valves and control equipment, enabling rapid deployment while supporting operational continuity, innovation and sustainability objectives.

tender.title: PROC 26-3336 Back-Office Solution for the Police Scotland EV Charging Infrastructure
tender.description:
Police Scotland currently have in place back-office services with two separate Suppliers, due to expire within the next 12 months. Police Scotland require a single Supplier to migrate all chargers from existing Contract to a new single Contract.
Police Scotland require a Supplier to provide a Single Back-Office Solution for the Police Scotland EV Charging Infrastructure; this will involve transitioning groups of chargers from these current solutions as well as adding any newly installed chargers added to the Estate during the Contract term, placed immediately on to this new Contract.

lots.description:
Police Scotland currently have in place back-office services with two separate Suppliers, due to expire within the next 12 months. Police Scotland require a single Supplier to migrate all chargers from existing Contracts to a new single Contract.
Police Scotland require a Supplier to provide a Single Back-Office Solution for the Police Scotland EV Charging Infrastructure; this will involve transitioning groups of chargers from these current solutions as well as adding any newly installed chargers added to the Estate during the Contract term, placed immediately on to this new Contract.
The Back Office functionality must provide a solution to manage the Authority’s electric vehicle charging infrastructure to allow control, visibility and development of the back-office solution. Software supplied must be able to provide data in-line with a standard back office system as well as allow utilisation of data as detailed within the Back Office section above. Software must provide charge point management software. Including live monitoring of charge point network, including charge sessions, access controls, management of tariffs and payments, maintenance and reporting.
Further information can be found within the Schedule of Requirements within the ITT document.
